siftei_kohen.he:
פרשת שמע והיה כו'. דכתיב בהו וכתבתם על מזוזות ביתך ובשעריך:
יאריכו ימיו כו'. דכתיב למען ירבו ימיכם וימי בניכם וגו':
siftei_kohen.en:
"He heard and was like." "You have written in your mouth and written about your house's exaggeration, and you are not afraid."
"His days are like him." It is written for the sake of your children and your children, and the days of your children, and the days of your children, and the days of your children, and the days of your children, and the days of your life, and the days of your children, and the blood of your children," he said

beur_hagra.he:
מ"ע כו'. מתני' מנחות כ"ח א' וע"ש ל"א ב': **** ENGLISH **** Positive commandment, etc. Mishnah Menachot 28a; and see there 31b.
וכל כו'. כמ"ש בפ"א דקדושין (ל"ד א'): **** ENGLISH **** And every, etc. — as written in chapter 1 of Kiddushin (34a).
וימי בניו כו'. כמ"ש פ"ב דשבת (ל"ב ב'): **** ENGLISH **** And the days of his sons, etc. — as written in chapter 2 of Shabbat (32b).
ומ"מ כו'. ירושלמי סוף מגילה תפילה ומזוזה מי קודמת שמואל אמר מזוזה קודמת רב הונא אמר תפלה קודמת מאי טעמא דשמואל שכן היא נוהגת בי"ט ובשבתות מ"ט דר"ה שכ"ה נוהגת במפרשי ימים והולכי מדברות מתני' מסייע לשמואל תפילה שבלה עושין אותה מזוזה מזוזה שבלתה אין עושין אותה תפלין למה שמעלין בקדש ולא מורידין ופסק הרא"ש כר"ה דמצוה דגופיה עדיף ודבריו תמוהין דטעם זה לא הוזכר כלל שם (וע' בחדושי רע"ק) והכריע מדעתו אלא יש לומר משום דההיא ברייתא איתמר בגמ' דידן (שבת ע"ט ב' ובמנחות) להיפך והיא מסייעא לר"ה ועבא"ח סי' ל"ח סי"ב: **** ENGLISH **** Nevertheless, etc. Yerushalmi end of Megillah — "tefillin and mezuzah — which precedes? Shmuel said mezuzah precedes; Rav Huna said tefillin precedes. What is Shmuel's reason? For so it is practiced on festivals and Sabbaths. What is R. Huna's reason? For so it is practiced by seafarers and desert travelers." Mishnah supports Shmuel — "worn-out tefillin one makes them into a mezuzah; worn-out mezuzah one does not make them into tefillin — why? We elevate in sanctity and do not lower." Rosh ruled like R. Huna, that bodily mitzvah takes precedence; and his words are astonishing, for this reason was not mentioned at all there (and see in Chiddushei Ra'ak). And he decided from his own view — one must say because that baraita was stated in our Gemara (Shabbat 79b and Menachot) to the contrary, and it supports R. Huna; and Orach Chaim siman 38 seif 12.

And the days of his sons, etc. — as written in chapter 2 of Shabbat (32b).
Nevertheless, etc. Yerushalmi end of Megillah — "tefillin and mezuzah — which precedes? Shmuel said mezuzah precedes; Rav Huna said tefillin precedes. What is Shmuel's reason? Mishnah supports Shmuel — "worn-out tefillin one makes them into a mezuzah; worn-out mezuzah one does not make them into tefillin — why? We elevate in sanctity and do not lower." Rosh ruled like R. pitchei_teshuva.he: מצות עשה לכתוב. נראה שאין כופין על מ"ע זו דהוי מצות עשה שמתן שכרה בצדה דכתיב וכתבתם כו' למען ירבו ימיכם ועיין בנ"צ לעיל סימן רמ"ה ס"ד הארכתי בזה. ועיין פמ"ג לאו"ח סי' ל"א דאם נודע לו בשבת וי"ט שאין מזוזה בפתחו ויש לו בית אחר מחוייב הוא לצאת אבל אי לית ליה בית אחר שרי לדור בתוכו דומיא דציצית בסימן י"ג ע"ש ונראה דה"ה אפילו בחול אם אין מזוזה נמצא בעיר דינו כמו בשבת ורשאי לדור בתוכו אם אין לו בית אחר כמה שכתב המג"א בסימן י"ג סק"ח לענין ציצית וע' במג"א סי' י"כו סק"א ודו"ק: **** ENGLISH **** Positive commandment to write. It appears one does not compel for this positive commandment, for it is a positive commandment whose reward is alongside it, as it is written "and you shall write them… that your days may be multiplied"; and see Netziv above siman 245 seif 4 where I elaborated on this. And see Pri Megadim Orach Chaim siman 31 — if on Shabbat or festival it became known to him there is no mezuzah on his doorway and he has another house — he is obligated to leave; but if he has no other house, it is permitted to dwell within, similar to tzitzit in siman 13 — see there. And it appears the same even on weekdays — if no mezuzah is found in the city, his law is like on Shabbat, and he is permitted to dwell within if he has no other house, as Magen Avraham wrote in siman 13 s.k. 8 regarding tzitzit; and see Magen Avraham siman 126 s.k. 1 — understand well.
pitchei_teshuva.en:
Positive commandment to write. It appears one does not compel for this positive commandment, for it is a positive commandment whose reward is alongside it, as it is written "and you shall write them… that your days may be multiplied"; and see Netziv above siman 245 seif 4 where I elaborated on this. And see Pri Megadim Orach Chaim siman 31 — if on Shabbat or festival it became known to him there is no mezuzah on his doorway and he has another house — he is obligated to leave; but if he has no other house, it is permitted to dwell within, similar to tzitzit in siman 13 — see there. And it appears the same even on weekdays — if no mezuzah is found in the city, his law is like on Shabbat, and he is permitted to dwell within if he has no other house, as Magen Avraham wrote in siman 13 s.k. 8 regarding tzitzit; and see Magen Avraham siman 126 s.k. 1 — understand well.
He should buy tefillin. See Magen Avraham siman 38 s.k. 4, who wrote that for us, since we place them only at time of Shema and prayer — if possible through borrowing, mezuzah precedes; but if not possible through borrowing. And see in book Chomot Yerushalayim siman 265, who wrote if one wants to wear tefillin all day and cannot borrow all day — requires study which precedes — see there. And see responsum in Orach Chaim siman 25 s.k. 1, who wrote regarding tzitzit and tefillin — the later authorities wrote that if it is possible to have tefillin through borrowing, tzitzit precede; and he wrote: it appears this means if his heart is sure he can borrow tefillin every day so at least he will not need to return them as long as he wishes, if others do not become available to buy; but if still there is concern perhaps he will need to return them before others become available — behold he is nullified from the mitzvah of tefillin which precedes tzitzit — end quote. And if so, the same for tefillin and mezuzah — if he is not sure he will have tefillin every day through borrowing, tefillin precede. But in my opinion requires study — for perhaps that tefillin precede mezuzah and tzitzit applies only when certainly if he does not buy tefillin he will certainly be nullified from tefillin; but not that his doubt removes their certainty — such as here, that if he does not buy tefillin perhaps he can still fulfill tefillin through borrowing — perhaps mezuzah and tzitzit precede, for if he buys tefillin he will certainly be nullified from mezuzah and tzitzit; but if he buys mezuzah and tzitzit perhaps he can also fulfill tefillin; and if so, even if he is not sure he will have tefillin every day, nevertheless mezuzah and tzitzit precede. Nevertheless, even if we say so, it appears specifically when he needs a mezuzah in his own house (and likewise tzitzit in his own tallit — see Orach Chaim siman 14 seif 3); but one who rents a house — for his obligation in mezuzah after thirty days is only rabbinic — all the more so below end siman 286 it is obvious that tefillin's doubt precedes this mezuzah's certainty, as written in Orach Chaim siman 495 regarding shofar and prayer. Further requires study — if he buys tefillin he is nullified from two mitzvot of mezuzah and tzitzit whose value is small and he cannot have tefillin through borrowing — which of them precedes. Further wrote in book of responsa — if he has tefillin of Rashi and wants to place tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam also and has no tzitzit — tzitzit precede, since most people do not place Rabbeinu Tam tefillin at all; but the reverse — if he has Rabbeinu Tam and not Rashi — they precede tzitzit, etc. — see there; and the same for mezuzah.

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (סימן רפ"ה סעיף א' בהגה"ה) דמצוה שהיא חובת הגוף עדיפא. נ"ל בפשוטו דהכוונה דהתפילין הוא חוב המוטל על גופו ואין לו אופן לפטור ממנה אבל מזוזה אין החיוב עליו לבנות בית ולקבוע מזוזה רק אם יש לו בית צריך לעשו' בו מזוזה כדאמרינן מזוזה חובת הדר הוא מש"ה תפילין קודמים ודומה לזה כ' בהג"ה בא"ח (סי' י"ז) ע"ש וראיתי לבית הלל שכ' בפשט הרמ"א דתפילין חובת הגוף היינו שהוא מלבוש והמצוה על גופו ממש משא"כ במזוזה ומזה כתב דה"ה דתפילין קודמין למצות סוכה ולולב דג"כ הוי לגבייהו חובת הגוף וכן לגבי ציצית ולענ"ד העיקר כמ"ש משא"כ לגבי סוכה ולולב אפשר דסוכה עדיף דחוב ג"כ עליו בליל ראשון וכן לולב רק לגבי ציצית נראה דהדין עמו דדמי ממש למזוזה דלא הוי חוב על הגוף רק אם לבוש טלית צריך לעשות ציצית כנלע"ד. אחר זה ראיתי בירושל' שמקור הדין יוצא ממנו ומצאתי להדיא כמ"ש והכי איתא התם מ"ט דר"ה שכן היא נוהגת במפרשי ימים והולכי מדבריות ע"ש והיינו כמ"ש דתפילין אין לו להנצל אבל במזוזה אפשר שהוא בים ואין עליו חיוב כלל משא"כ בלולב דגם בים החיוב עליו והוא ברור. אולם יש לדון מטעם אחר דתפילין קודמים לסוכה ולולב והיינו דתפילין הוא מ"ע הנוהג כל השנה ולולב הוא רק פעם א' בשנה וכמו דס"ל לשמואל בירושלמי דס' מזוזה קודמת לתפילין דמזוזה נוהגת אף בשבת ויו"ט משא"כ תפילין (והוי תדיר ושאינו תדיר) אלא דר"ה פליג עלה וס"ל דתפילין שהוא חובת הגוף עדיף וא"כ תפילין ולולב דשניהם חובת הגוף הדרי' לסברא דאידך מ"ד כיון דתפילין נוהג כל השנה תפילין קודם ודוקא בתפילין ולולב אבל ציצית ולולב נ"ל דלולב קודם לציצית אף דציצית כל השנה מ"מ הא לולב חובת הגוף וכמ"ש כנלע"ד: והא דפסקינן כר"ה לגבי שמואל דתפילין קודמין למזוזה ע' בהרא"ש הלכות תפילין שכ' ומסתברא דהלכה כר"ה דמצוה דגופא עדיף וגם מפרש תלמודא טעמיה וע' קרבן עדה שהשיג על זה וכתב טעם אחר לפסוק כר"ה ולעד"נ טעם אחר לפסוק כר"ה ויבואר ג"כ אופן מחלקותם דשמואל ור"ה ונעתיק לשון הירושלמי וז"ל תפילין ומזוזה מי קודם שמואל אמר מזוזה קודמת ר"ה אמר תפילין קודמת מ"ט דשמואל שכן היא נוהגת בימים טובים ושבתות מ"מ דר"ה שכן היא נוהגת במפרשי ימים והולכי מדבריות מתני' מסייע לשמואל תפלה שבלה עושין אותה מזוזה מזוזה שבלתה אין עושין אותה תפלה למה שמעלין בקדש ולא מורידים עכ"ל הירושלמי ונראה דמחלוקתם דשמואל ור"ה תליא בזה במה דמבואר בזבחים (צ"א) דרצה הש"ס למפשט דתדיר ומקודש מקודש קודם ממתני' דשלמים של אמש וחטאת ואשם של היום השלמים קודמים והא אידי ואידי דיום חטאת ואשם קדמי ואע"ג דשלמים תדירי אמר רבא מצוי קאמרת תדיר קמיבעיא לן מצוי לא קמיבעיא לן (פירש"י מצוי קאמרת שאין תדירתו חובה אלא שהוא מצוי תמיד יותר מחבירו) א"ל ר"ה בר' יהודה לרבא אטו מצוי לאו תדיר הוא ע"ש הרי מבואר דרבא ס"ל דמצוי לא מקרי תדיר כיון שאין תדירתו חובה ור"ה בר"י ס"ל דהוי תדיר א"כ י"ל דשמואל ס' כר"ה בר"י ומש"ה ס"ל דמזוזה קודם שנוהג אף בשבתות ויו"ט דהוי תדיר לגבי תפילין ור"ה סבר כרבא דמצוי לא הוי תדיר וממילא הוי תפילין שנוהג עכ"פ בימות החול לחוב ומזוזה אפשר כל השנה בלא מזוזה דאם רוצה יהיה במפרשי ימים וה"מ וזה דקאמר בירושלמי בטעמיה דר"ה שכן היא נוהגת במפ"י ובה"מ היינו דמכח זה הוי תפילין תדיר דמזוזה הוא רק מצוי ולא תדיר (ומה"ט כתב בת' שאגת אריה דספירת העומר קודם לבהמ"ז בחול דספירת העומר הוי תדיר לגבי בהמ"ז דאי בעי לא אכל ע"ש) אף דמצינו רק דתדיר ושאינו תדיר תדיר קודם היינו אם שניהם לפניו ולהקדים א' לחבירו אבל הכא בתפילין ומזוזה שהוא נדחה מחבירו ל"ש תדיר קודם מ"מ גם בזה לענין לדחות תדיר קודם כמ"ש הרא"ש (פ"ב דשבת סי' י"ב) דתדיר קודם אפי' לדחות את שא"ת וכן נראה בפשיטות בסוכה (נ"ד ע"ב) תוספות ד"ה ואמאי תדיר וכו' וכיון שכן למה דמסקי' בזבחים שם כרבא דמצוי לא מקרי תדיר ממילא קי"ל כר"ה דתפילין קודמים ומלבד פירושינו כדברי הירושלמי נ"ל דהראיה נכונה לפסוק כד"ה ותפילין קודמים מטעם דהוי תדיר לגבי מזוזה ואף דהוא איבעיא דלא איפשיטא בזבחים אם מקודש קודם לתדיר מ"מ הא קיי"ל דתפילין יותד קדוש ממזוזה כדאיתא בש"ע לקמן (סי' ר"ץ ס"א) עיי"ש: וע"פ דברינו מיושב היטב הראיה שכתב הירושלמי תפילין שבלה כו' דלכאורה מאי ראיה היא זו דמ"מ י"ל דלענין מצוה דמצוה דגופא עדיף ולדברינו ניחא דעיקר סברא דר"ה דתפילין הוי תדיר לגבי מזוזה ולזה שפיר קאמר הירושלמי דאף אם נניח סברת ר"ה דתפילין הוי תדיר מ"מ מזוזה עדיף כיון דמקודש יותר וס"ל להירושלמי בפשטות דמקודש ותדיר מקודש קודם ומ"מ אנן פסקינן כר"ה כיון דקיי"ל דתפילין מקודש יותר ממזוזה וק"ל: **** ENGLISH **** (Siman 285 seif 1 in Hagahah) That it is a bodily obligation takes precedence. It appears in the plain sense the intent is that tefillin is an obligation placed on his body and he has no way to exempt himself from it; but mezuzah — the obligation is not upon him to build a house and affix a mezuzah, only if he has a house he must make a mezuzah in it, as we say "mezuzah is an obligation of dwelling" — therefore tefillin precede. And similar to this he wrote in Hagahah in Orach Chaim (siman 17) — see there. And I saw in Beit HaLevi who wrote per the plain sense of Rama — tefillin is bodily obligation, meaning it is a garment and the mitzvah is literally on his body, unlike mezuzah; and from this he wrote that likewise tefillin precede sukkah and lulav, for they too are bodily obligations relative to him; and likewise regarding tzitzit. And in my humble opinion the essence is as written — unlike sukkah and lulav, where perhaps sukkah takes precedence for he is also obligated on the first night, and likewise lulav; only regarding tzitzit the law is with him, for it is truly like mezuzah — it is not an obligation on the body, only if he wears a tallit garment he must make tzitzit — so it appears to me. Afterward I saw in Yerushalmi that the source of this law emerges from it, and I found explicitly as written — and so it is stated there: "What is R. Huna's reason? For so it is practiced by seafarers and desert travelers" — see there; and this is as written — that with tefillin he has no way to exempt himself, but with mezuzah it is possible he is at sea and has no obligation at all, unlike lulav where even at sea the obligation is upon him — and this is clear. However one may argue from another reason that tefillin precede sukkah and lulav — namely tefillin is a positive commandment practiced all year, and lulav only once a year; and as Shmuel holds in Yerushalmi that mezuzah precedes tefillin, for mezuzah is practiced even on Shabbat and festivals unlike tefillin (and this is frequent versus infrequent); except R. Huna disputes and holds tefillin, being bodily obligation, takes precedence; and if so tefillin and lulav, both being obligations of dwelling — per the other's view: since tefillin are practiced all year, tefillin precede; and specifically tefillin and lulav; but tzitzit and lulav — it appears to me lulav precedes tzitzit, although tzitzit all year, nevertheless lulav is bodily obligation — as written, so it appears to me. And that we rule like R. Huna against Shmuel that tefillin precede mezuzah — see in Rosh Laws of Tefillin, who wrote it is reasonable the halachah is like R. Huna that bodily mitzvah takes precedence, and Gemara too explains his reason; and see Korban Eidah who challenged this and wrote another reason to rule like R. Huna; and in my humble opinion another reason to rule like R. Huna, and the manner of their dispute between Shmuel and R. Huna will also be explained. And I will quote Yerushalmi's language: "Tefillin and mezuzah — which precedes? Shmuel said mezuzah precedes; R. Huna said tefillin precedes. What is Shmuel's reason? For so it is practiced on festivals and Sabbaths. What is R. Huna's reason? For so it is practiced by seafarers and desert travelers. Mishnah supports Shmuel — worn-out tefillin one makes them into a mezuzah; worn-out mezuzah one does not make them into tefillin — why? We elevate in sanctity and do not lower" — end Yerushalmi. And it appears their dispute between Shmuel and R. Huna depends on what is explained in Zevachim (91) — Gemara wanted to establish that frequent and sanctified — sanctified precedes, from mishnah "peace-offerings of yesterday and sin-offering and guilt-offering of today — peace-offerings precede"; but both are of the day — sin-offering and guilt-offering precede; and although peace-offerings are more frequent, Rava said "you say frequent? We are in doubt about frequent, we are not in doubt about common" (Rashi explained: you say common — its frequency is not obligatory but it is always more available than its fellow). R. Huna son of R. Yehuda said to Rava: is common not frequent? — see there. Behold it is clear Rava holds common is not called frequent since its frequency is not obligatory; and R. Huna son of R. Yehuda holds it is frequent. If so, one may say Shmuel holds like R. Huna son of R. Yehuda, and therefore holds mezuzah precedes, for it is practiced even on Sabbaths and festivals — which is frequent relative to tefillin; and R. Huna holds like Rava that common is not frequent; automatically tefillin which are practiced at least on weekdays are obligatory, and mezuzah perhaps all year without mezuzah — for if he wishes he will be among seafarers and desert travelers — and this is what Yerushalmi says in R. Huna's reason "for so it is practiced by seafarers and desert travelers" — meaning through this tefillin are frequent and mezuzah is only common and not frequent (and for this reason Sefer Sha'agat Aryeh wrote counting the omer precedes musaf on weekdays, for counting the omer is frequent relative to musaf — for if he wishes he will not eat — see there). Although we find only that frequent and infrequent — frequent precedes — meaning if both are before him to precede one over the other; but here with tefillin and mezuzah where one is deferred from the other, frequent precedes has no relevance; nevertheless also for deferring, frequent precedes, as Rosh wrote (chapter 2 of Shabbat siman 12) — frequent precedes even to defer the infrequent; and so appears plainly in Sukkah (54b) Tosafot s.v. ve'ama'i frequent, etc. And since we conclude in Zevachim there like Rava that common is not called frequent — automatically we hold like R. Huna that tefillin precede. And besides our explanation per Yerushalmi's words, it appears to me the proof is correct to rule per "and tefillin precede" — because tefillin are frequent relative to mezuzah; and although it is an unresolved question in Zevachim whether sanctified precedes frequent, nevertheless we hold tefillin are more sanctified than mezuzah, as stated in Shulchan Aruch below (siman 291 seif 1) — see there. And per our words the proof that Yerushalmi wrote "worn-out tefillin," etc. is well settled — for at first glance what proof is this? Nevertheless one may say for bodily mitzvah takes precedence; and per our words it is proper — the essence of R. Huna's reasoning is that tefillin are frequent relative to mezuzah; and for this Yerushalmi properly says that even if we grant R. Huna's view that tefillin are frequent, nevertheless mezuzah takes precedence since it is more sanctified; and Yerushalmi plainly holds sanctified and frequent — sanctified precedes; and nevertheless we rule like R. Huna since we hold tefillin are more sanctified than mezuzah — understand well.
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: (Siman 285 seif 1 in Hagahah) That it is a bodily obligation takes precedence. It appears in the plain sense the intent is that tefillin is an obligation placed on his body and he has no way to exempt himself from it; but mezuzah — the obligation is not upon him to build a house and affix a mezuzah, only if he has a house he must make a mezuzah in it, as we say "mezuzah is an obligation of dwelling" — therefore tefillin precede. And similar to this he wrote in Hagahah in Orach Chaim (siman 17) — see there. And I saw in Beit HaLevi who wrote per the plain sense of Rama — tefillin is bodily obligation, meaning it is a garment and the mitzvah is literally on his body, unlike mezuzah; and from this he wrote that likewise tefillin precede sukkah and lulav, for they too are bodily obligations relative to him; and likewise regarding tzitzit. And in my humble opinion the essence is as written — unlike sukkah and lulav, where perhaps sukkah takes precedence for he is also obligated on the first night, and likewise lulav; only regarding tzitzit the law is with him, for it is truly like mezuzah — it is not an obligation on the body, only if he wears a tallit garment he must make tzitzit — so it appears to me. Afterward I saw in Yerushalmi that the source of this law emerges from it, and I found explicitly as written — and so it is stated there: "What is R. Huna's reason? For so it is practiced by seafarers and desert travelers" — see there; and this is as written — that with tefillin he has no way to exempt himself, but with mezuzah it is possible he is at sea and has no obligation at all, unlike lulav where even at sea the obligation is upon him — and this is clear. However one may argue from another reason that tefillin precede sukkah and lulav — namely tefillin is a positive commandment practiced all year, and lulav only once a year; and as Shmuel holds in Yerushalmi that mezuzah precedes tefillin, for mezuzah is practiced even on Shabbat and festivals unlike tefillin (and this is frequent versus infrequent); except R. Huna disputes and holds tefillin, being bodily obligation, takes precedence; and if so tefillin and lulav, both being obligations of dwelling — per the other's view: since tefillin are practiced all year, tefillin precede; and specifically tefillin and lulav; but tzitzit and lulav — it appears to me lulav precedes tzitzit, although tzitzit all year, nevertheless lulav is bodily obligation — as written, so it appears to me. And that we rule like R. Huna against Shmuel that tefillin precede mezuzah — see in Rosh Laws of Tefillin, who wrote it is reasonable the halachah is like R. Huna that bodily mitzvah takes precedence, and Gemara too explains his reason; and see Korban Eidah who challenged this and wrote another reason to rule like R. Huna; and in my humble opinion another reason to rule like R. Huna, and the manner of their dispute between Shmuel and R. Huna will also be explained. And I will quote Yerushalmi's language: "Tefillin and mezuzah — which precedes? Shmuel said mezuzah precedes; R. Huna said tefillin precedes. What is Shmuel's reason? For so it is practiced on festivals and Sabbaths. What is R. Huna's reason? For so it is practiced by seafarers and desert travelers. Mishnah supports Shmuel — worn-out tefillin one makes them into a mezuzah; worn-out mezuzah one does not make them into tefillin — why? We elevate in sanctity and do not lower" — end Yerushalmi. And it appears their dispute between Shmuel and R. Huna depends on what is explained in Zevachim (91) — Gemara wanted to establish that frequent and sanctified — sanctified precedes, from mishnah "peace-offerings of yesterday and sin-offering and guilt-offering of today — peace-offerings precede"; but both are of the day — sin-offering and guilt-offering precede; and although peace-offerings are more frequent, Rava said "you say frequent? We are in doubt about frequent, we are not in doubt about common" (Rashi explained: you say common — its frequency is not obligatory but it is always more available than its fellow). R. Huna son of R. Yehuda said to Rava: is common not frequent? — see there. Behold it is clear Rava holds common is not called frequent since its frequency is not obligatory; and R. Huna son of R. Yehuda holds it is frequent. If so, one may say Shmuel holds like R. Huna son of R. Yehuda, and therefore holds mezuzah precedes, for it is practiced even on Sabbaths and festivals — which is frequent relative to tefillin; and R. Huna holds like Rava that common is not frequent; automatically tefillin which are practiced at least on weekdays are obligatory, and mezuzah perhaps all year without mezuzah — for if he wishes he will be among seafarers and desert travelers — and this is what Yerushalmi says in R. pitchei_teshuva.he: יקנה תפלין. עיין במג"א סימן ל"ח סק"ד שכתב דלדידן שאין מניחין רק בשעת ק"ש ותפלה אם אפשר בשאלה מזוזה קודמת. דאי אפשר בשאלה ועיין בספר חומות ירושלים סוס"י רס"ה שכתב דאם רוצה ללבוש תפילין כל היום וא"א בשאלה לכל היום צ"ע הי קדים ע"ש. ועיין בש"ת בא"ח סימן כ"ה סק"א שכתב לענין ציצית ותפילין שכתבו האחרונים שאם אפשר שיהיה לו תפילין בשאלה ציצית קודמין וז"ל ונראה דהיינו אם נכון לבו בטוח שיוכל לשאול תפילין בכל יום שעכ"פ לא יהיה צריך להחזירם כ"ז שירצה אם לא יזדמנו לו לקנות ואם לא אכתי איכא למיחש שמא יצטרך להחזירם טרם שיזדמנו לו אחרים ונמצא בטל ממצות תפילין שהוא קודם לציצית עכ"ל. וא"כ ה"ה לענין תפילין ומזוזה אם אינו בטוח שיהיה לו תפילין בכל יום בשאלה תפילין קודמין. אך לדעתי צ"ע דאפשר הא דתפילין קודמים למזוזה וציצית דוקא ודאי דתפילין מודאי דמזוזה וציצית היינו היכא שאם לא יקנה תפילין יתבטל בודאי ממצות תפילין אבל לא שיהא ספיקא דידיה מוציא מידי ודאי שלהם כגון הכא שאם לא יקנה תפילין אפשר שיקיים גם מצות תפילין בשאלה אולי מזוזה וציצית קודמין דאם יקנה תפילין יתבטל בודאי ממזוזה וציצית אבל אם יקנה מזוזה וציצית אפשר שיקיים גם מצות תפילין וא"כ אף אם אינו בטוח שיהיו לו תפילין בכל יום מכל מקום מזוזה וציצית קודמין ומ"מ אף אם נאמר כן נראה דדוקא באם צריך למזוזה בבית שלו (וכן בציצית בטלית שלו עיין בא"ח סימן י"ד ס"ג) אבל בשוכר בית דהא דחייב במזוזה אחר ל' הוא רק מדרבנן כ"ש לקמן סוף סימן רפ"ו פשיטא דספיקא דתפילין קודם לודאי זו דמזוזה כמ"ש בא"ח סימן תקצ"ה בענין שופר ותפלה. עוד צ"ע באם יקנה תפילין יתבטל משתי מצות מזוזה וציצית שדמיהן מועטין ולא אפשר לו תפילין בשאלה איזה מהם קודם. עוד כתב בס' ש"ת דאם יש לו תפילין של רש"י ורוצה להניח תפילין של ר"ת ג"כ ואין לו ציצית הציצית קודמין כיון דרובי דאינשי אין מניחין תפילין של ר"ת כלל אבל איפכא לא דאם יש לו של ר"ת ואין לו של רש"י הם קודמין לציצית כו' ע"ש וה"ה למזוזה: **** ENGLISH **** He should buy tefillin. See Magen Avraham siman 38 s.k. 4, who wrote that for us, since we place them only at time of Shema and prayer — if possible through borrowing, mezuzah precedes; but if not possible through borrowing. And see in book Chomot Yerushalayim siman 265, who wrote if one wants to wear tefillin all day and cannot borrow all day — requires study which precedes — see there. And see responsum in Orach Chaim siman 25 s.k. 1, who wrote regarding tzitzit and tefillin — the later authorities wrote that if it is possible to have tefillin through borrowing, tzitzit precede; and he wrote: it appears this means if his heart is sure he can borrow tefillin every day so at least he will not need to return them as long as he wishes, if others do not become available to buy; but if still there is concern perhaps he will need to return them before others become available — behold he is nullified from the mitzvah of tefillin which precedes tzitzit — end quote. And if so, the same for tefillin and mezuzah — if he is not sure he will have tefillin every day through borrowing, tefillin precede. But in my opinion requires study — for perhaps that tefillin precede mezuzah and tzitzit applies only when certainly if he does not buy tefillin he will certainly be nullified from tefillin; but not that his doubt removes their certainty — such as here, that if he does not buy tefillin perhaps he can still fulfill tefillin through borrowing — perhaps mezuzah and tzitzit precede, for if he buys tefillin he will certainly be nullified from mezuzah and tzitzit; but if he buys mezuzah and tzitzit perhaps he can also fulfill tefillin; and if so, even if he is not sure he will have tefillin every day, nevertheless mezuzah and tzitzit precede. Nevertheless, even if we say so, it appears specifically when he needs a mezuzah in his own house (and likewise tzitzit in his own tallit — see Orach Chaim siman 14 seif 3); but one who rents a house — for his obligation in mezuzah after thirty days is only rabbinic — all the more so below end siman 286 it is obvious that tefillin's doubt precedes this mezuzah's certainty, as written in Orach Chaim siman 495 regarding shofar and prayer. Further requires study — if he buys tefillin he is nullified from two mitzvot of mezuzah and tzitzit whose value is small and he cannot have tefillin through borrowing — which of them precedes. Further wrote in book of responsa — if he has tefillin of Rashi and wants to place tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam also and has no tzitzit — tzitzit precede, since most people do not place Rabbeinu Tam tefillin at all; but the reverse — if he has Rabbeinu Tam and not Rashi — they precede tzitzit, etc. — see there; and the same for mezuzah.
